title: China’s Anti-Corruption Campaign Roils On - The Wire China
gist: Fang Xinghai, 62, former vice-chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, was placed under investigation for 'suspected serious disciplinary and legal violations' by China's Central Commission for Discipline Inspection on July 24, 2026, and was absent (represented only by an empty nameplate) from a scheduled keynote at a Beijing conference the following month.

themes.theme: CSRC's anti-corruption probe reaches former leadership

insights.claim: Fang Xinghai, former vice-chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), was placed under investigation on July 24, 2026 by the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection for 'suspected serious disciplinary and legal violations.'
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: A former top securities regulator becoming a target of China's anti-corruption campaign signals the graft probe is extending into the financial-regulatory apparatus itself, not just industry or party officials — a signal to watch for further CSRC-linked personnel moves or policy reviews.
insights.quote: China’s top graft buster announced Fang was under investigation for “suspected serious disciplinary and legal violations.”

insights.claim: Fang Xinghai, 62, was scheduled to deliver a keynote address at a Beijing conference last month, but he was absent and only a nameplate marked his place, following the announcement of his investigation the evening before.
insights.speaker: Ella Apostoaie
insights.so_what: The empty-nameplate optics illustrate how abruptly and publicly Chinese officials under investigation are pulled from public/financial-sector events, a visible early tell investors can watch for future anti-corruption actions against sitting or former financial regulators.
insights.quote: Fang Xinghai, former vice-chairman of China Securities Regulatory Commission, was scheduled to give a keynote address at a conference in Beijing last month, but in his place there was only a nameplate.
